transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been feeling really paranoid lately, like I'm constantly being watched and monitored by people. It's making me feel deeply depressed and sad, and it feels like it's been going on for months now.
Have you been experiencing any hearing or seeing things that others cannot, such as voices or visions, alongside these feelings of being watched?

Yes, I have been. For about nine months now, I've been hearing whispering voices when I'm alone, and sometimes I see shadowy figures moving in the room. It's really terrifying because no one else can see or hear them, and it just makes me feel even more unsafe.
Did the feelings of depression and sadness start around the same time as the whispering voices and shadowy figures, or were they present before these hallucinations began?

The voices and shadowy figures actually started first, about nine months ago. The deep sadness and depression didn't develop until about two months later, around seven months ago. So I was dealing with those scary experiences for a while before the depression set in.

Would you say that the depressive symptoms, such as the deep sadness, have been continuously present and prominent throughout the past seven months, or have they been intermittent or less prominent compared to the psychotic symptoms?

The deep sadness and depression have been continuously present and very heavy for the entire past seven months. It feels like a constant cloud that never really lifts, even while I'm still dealing with the voices and shadows.
Have there been any periods where you've had at least two weeks without any significant psychotic symptoms, such as hearing voices or seeing things, but still experienced depressive symptoms?
No, there haven't been any times like that. Ever since the depression started seven months ago, the voices and shadowy figures have been there right along with it. They haven't
Can you think of any times when your mood was okay, but you were still experiencing the voices or shadowy figures, or have the psychotic symptoms always been accompanied by depressive symptoms?

Yes, actually. Right before the depression really hit me seven months ago, there was a period of about two or three weeks where my mood felt relatively okay, but I was still hearing the whispers and seeing the shadows. Even though I didn't feel deeply sad during that brief time, those scary experiences were still happening constantly.

During that two or three week period when your mood felt relatively okay, did the voices and shadowy figures seem to have any impact on your daily functioning or relationships, or were you able to manage them without much interference?

Even though my mood was okay, the voices and shadows still made it really hard to function. I was constantly distracted and terrified, which made it difficult to focus on my work or talk to my family. I ended up isolating myself quite a bit because I felt so unsafe.

For most of the time over the past nine months, have the psychotic symptoms, such as the voices and shadows, been the dominant symptoms, or have the depressive symptoms been more prominent in interfering with your life?

I would say the depressive symptoms have been the most prominent and have interfered with my life the most. The constant sadness and total lack of energy make it almost impossible to function, even more so than the voices. It really feels like the depression has dominated the majority of the time.
Have there been any periods where the depressive symptoms, such as the deep sadness, significantly improved or remitted, but the psychotic symptoms, like the voices and shadows, persisted?

Yes, there was a period of about three weeks where the deep sadness actually lifted and I felt emotionally much better. But even though my mood had improved during that time, the whispering voices and the shadowy figures were still happening just as much as before.

During that three-week period when your depressive symptoms improved, did you still meet the full criteria for a major depressive episode, or were there other significant symptoms present that dominated the clinical picture?

During those three weeks, my depressive symptoms had mostly cleared up, so I didn't feel fully depressed or sad anymore. However, the whispering voices, shadowy figures, and the feeling of being monitored continued just as strongly on their own. Those scary experiences were definitely the main things dominating my life during that time.
